summary.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

segments.name: Travel QSR
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth driven by throughput, menu engineering and value combos.

segments.name: Lounges
segments.commentary: About 41% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth from premiumisation and dwell time. Kyra Lounge opened at Hong Kong International Airport and a Cochin lounge opened in the year.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in the 80% to 83% range for FY27 overall, with some inflationary pressure from LPG prices linked to the Middle East conflict.
Capex averaging INR50 crore to INR60 crore a year, including FY27, mainly for unit mobilisation at Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida.
Receivables (about INR264 crore at year-end vs INR100-110 crore average) expected to normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.
Management expects FY27 passenger traffic growth of around 5%, per public reports, with Q1 FY27 still affected by the war-like situation.
Annual dividend of INR10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Bhogapuram (Vizag) contract under GHL expected to add about seven outlets; Noida airport operations expected to start in the coming months.
capex_capacity: Pipeline of more than 50 outlets, all committed per management.
Network now covers 20 airports and more than 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges; 76 travel QSR units mobilised in FY26 (including Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai).
Noida airport on track to start operations in the coming months; two more airports in the works in the coming months.
International: Malaysia lounges expanded to three airports; second Hong Kong lounge opened in Q4; subsidiaries in Dubai and Indonesia.
Delhi T3 concession expired in February 2026; a six-month short-term extension was granted, and the company plans to bid through its JV GHL when it comes up.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic at TFS airports grew 1.2% in FY26; Q4 was broadly flat YoY, with January up, February flat and March/April weaker on international traffic.
Management said domestic traffic was robust while international traffic fell nearly double digits in March-April, especially at southern airports and Goa.
Food inflation was about 3% to 5% in April per management; price hikes taken in line with inflation; key supplier contracts are annual.
Management said the mass-market credit card lounge access curbs are offset by premium cards growing more than 50%, with premium cardholders being frequent flyers.
Management expects LFL to be driven by about 7% to 10% passenger traffic plus about 7% to 10% from price and initiatives (combined).

qa_highlights.question: How is Q1 FY27 trading, given last year's Q1 was hit by India-Pakistan conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was strong, February was muted, March and April were weak on international traffic, and early May shows improving trends versus March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic growth in FY27 and risk from Kolkata airport privatisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not guide numbers; cited 11 airports in the privatisation pipeline and said Kolkata's inclusion or state changes are not expected to alter the schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can airport F&B pricing and energy costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric equipment is a large part of the cost base, giving a natural hedge; food inflation has been manageable, and price hikes follow inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Are airport concession fees rising and what is long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rentals are a normal portfolio negotiation with some going up and some down; management said nothing dramatically different is happening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structural versus temporary Q4 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-off reclassification of INR78 million cost reduced gross margin to 85.6% in Q4; full-year gross margin excluding it is about 84%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and what drove the receivables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to a INR212 million litigation provision booked in full; receivables rose on EATS bank billing ramp-up and should normalise by H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state LFL breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: LFL is roughly passenger traffic (7% to 10% historically) plus 7% to 10% from price and initiatives, averaged over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and interest in duty-free or retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stressed cash discipline, zero debt and ROCE of about 45%, and prioritised international lounges and expressway wayside amenities; no duty-free plans were mentioned.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and international traffic recovery; Gulf-bound and NRI travel remains weak.
Input cost pressure: LPG prices and food inflation impact on gross margin against the 80% to 83% range.
Receivables of about INR264 crore at year-end must normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27 as EATS scales.
Credit card lounge access restrictions from banks, a structural lounge risk.
Litigation provision of INR212 million, with the outcome still open; Delhi T3 concession extension expires after six months.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term aviation growth, but cautious on near-term traffic, citing the Middle East conflict and international traffic weakness. Management was evasive on specific FY27 inorganic growth and gave no numeric revenue guidance.
